chunks: “There was in al-Madinah a well in the middle of a garbage dump. The wind would blow and cast filth into it, and the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform wudu (ablution) from it.”

key_terms.الرِّيحُ: the wind that carried matter into the well
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: al-Madinah, the city where this occurred
key_terms.بِئْرٌ: a well used as a water source
key_terms.مَزْبَلَةٍ: a garbage dump or refuse place

ai.seo_question: Can water from a well remain pure for wudu (ablution) even if filth is blown into it?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that there was a well in al-Madinah exposed to surrounding refuse and windblown filth, yet the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used water from it for wudu (ablution). It is cited in the context of rulings on the purity of water and indicates the legal significance of water not being judged impure merely by nearby contamination.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.33 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"There was a well in Medina in the middle of a garbage dump. The wind would blow filth into it, yet The Prophet (sw) used to perform ablution from it."
